item.title: AI Security: OWASP LLM Top 10, Prompt Injection and Agent Security
item.description:
Simple definition#

AI security protects AI systems — models, prompts, data, tools and agents — from being manipulated, leaking information, or being used to cause harm. Classic application security still applies; LLMs add a new problem: instructions and data travel in the same channel (natural language), so data can act like code.

item.title: AI Governance and Responsible AI
item.description:
Simple definition#

AI governance is the set of policies, roles, processes and technical controls that make sure an organisation’s AI is lawful, safe, fair, secure, transparent and accountable — and that someone is answerable for each system. Responsible AI names the principles; governance is how you put them into practice.

item.title: Claude Code Hooks Reference
item.description:
Simple definition#

A hook is your own handler — a shell command, an HTTP endpoint, an MCP tool, or a model prompt — that Claude Code runs at a fixed point in its loop, such as before a tool call or when Claude tries to finish. Unlike CLAUDE.md, a command or HTTP hook is deterministic: the harness runs it every time, whatever the model decided. Hooks are how you make a rule hold with zero exceptions.

item.title: Claude Code Settings Reference
item.description:
Simple definition#

Claude Code reads JSON settings files at several levels — your user file, the project’s shared and local files, and the organisation’s managed settings — and combines them into one effective configuration. Settings control what Claude may do (permissions, sandbox), which model it uses, what loads into context, which extensions run, and what is reported. Environment variables cover authentication, providers and a few low-level limits.

item.title: Agentic AI Strategy and Operating Model
item.description:
Simple definition#

An agentic AI strategy decides where agents should do work in the organisation, how much autonomy they get, what platform they run on, how value and risk are measured, and how people and processes change around them. It turns isolated pilots into a governed, scalable capability.

item.title: Claude Code for Teams and Organisations
item.description:
Simple definition#

For a team, Claude Code configuration has three owners. The repository carries shared conventions, permissions, hooks, skills, agents and MCP servers, committed like any other code. Each developer keeps personal preferences in local and user files. The organisation sets policy through managed settings that no one else can override, and watches usage and spend through analytics and telemetry.

item.title: GenAI Adoption Strategy for the Enterprise
item.description:
Simple definition#

A GenAI adoption strategy decides where generative AI should create value, which capabilities the organisation buys or builds, which models and deployments it standardises on, how risk is governed, and how people and processes change — so that AI moves from scattered experiments to a measured, repeatable capability.

item.title: Using Claude Intelligently
item.description:
Simple definition#

Using Claude intelligently means getting reliable, verified results at the lowest sensible cost and risk. It rests on five habits: give the right context, ask for a clear outcome, make the result verifiable, pick the right model and effort, and keep a human accountable for what ships.
